query: For a Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy initially in a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-containing state, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain its subsequent microstructural evolution and the associated retention or loss of corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance? The hypothesis should address the unresolved transformation pathway and kinetics while accounting for the tendency of these alloys to develop intermetallic compounds. Specify an unnamed controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to the initial state, the relevant service-regime boundaries, supporting evidence from reported Mg-containing alloys, and a clear falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: In a metastable, as‐cast Mg–Fe–Al–Cr–Ti high‐entropy alloy (HEA), isothermal annealing at 500 °C triggers a two‐stage decomposition pathway—initial spinodal decomposition into Mg‐enriched and Mg‐depleted nanodomains within ~10 h, followed by nucleation and growth of ordered L12‐type intermetallic precipitates by 100 h—that produces a fine network of nano‐scale precipitates which impede oxygen and ion diffusion and thus retain or improve high‐temperature oxidation and aqueous corrosion resistance relative to the as‐cast state.
generation.material_initial_state: as‐cast, non‐equilibrium, metastable solid‐solution Mg–Fe–Al–Cr–Ti HEA
generation.intervention: isothermal annealing at 500 °C for controlled durations (10 h and 100 h)
generation.conditions: 500 °C in inert atmosphere, ±10 °C control; total annealing times 0–100 h
generation.structural_mediator: volume fraction and size distribution of ordered L12‐type intermetallic precipitates inside grains
generation.mechanism: diffusion‐controlled spinodal decomposition of Mg‐rich domains and subsequent atomic ordering to L12 phases
generation.predicted_outcome: after 100 h at 500 °C: ~20–40% reduction in high‐temperature oxidation mass gain (500 °C, 100 h) and ~50 mV nobler corrosion potential in 3.5 wt% NaCl vs. as‐cast baseline
generation.baseline: as‐cast metastable solid‐solution state without annealing
generation.boundary: valid for service and heat‐treatment temperatures between 300 °C and 600 °C and times up to ~100 h
generation.uncertainty: exact kinetics (time‐to‐spinodal onset, L12 nucleation rate) and numeric magnitude of corrosion/oxidation gains are estimated from analogous Mg‐containing alloys

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare identical as‐cast HEA specimens, anneal subsets at 500 °C for 10 h and 100 h, then (a) perform TEM to quantify L12 precipitate volume fraction and size, and (b) measure oxidation mass gain after 100 h at 500 °C and corrosion potential in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
measurements: TEM precipitate volume fraction and size distribution
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If after 100 h at 500 °C the L12 precipitate volume fraction does not exceed 10% or the oxidation mass gain remains within ±5% of the as‐cast baseline (and corrosion potential shifts <20 mV), then the hypothesis is falsified.
